content.overview: BNS s. 208 — Non-attendance in obedience to an order from public servant.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Non-attendance in obedience to an order from public servant. BNS restatement of IPC 174. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 174. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 208 is the rule on “Non-attendance in obedience to an order from public servant”. The section provides that whoever, being legally bound to attend in person or by an agent at a certain place and time in obedience to a summons, notice, order, or proclamation proceeding from any public servant legally competent, as such public servant, to issue the same, intentionally omits to attend at that place or time or departs from the place where he is bound to attend before the time at which it is lawful for him to depart,–. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 208 exists so that “Non-attendance in obedience to an order from public servant” has a closed legal test in Chapter XIII — Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Summons, proclamations, false information — and the recast suicide-attempt-to-coerce offence.

The provision in detail
208. Whoever, being legally bound to attend in person or by an agent at a certain place and time in obedience to a summons, notice, order, or proclamation proceeding from any public servant legally competent, as such public servant, to issue the same, intentionally omits to attend at that place or time or departs from the place where he is bound to attend before the time at which it is lawful for him to depart,–

(a) shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both;

(b) where the summons, notice, order or proclamation is to attend in person or by agent in a Court with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever, being legally bound to attend in person or by an agent at a certain place and time in obedience to a summons, notice, order, or proclamation proceeding from any public servant legally competent, as such public servant, to issue the same, intentionally omits to attend at that place or time or departs from the place where he is bound to attend before the time at which it is lawful for him to depart,–
2. (a) shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both;
3. (b) where the summons, notice, order or proclamation is to attend in person or by agent in a Court with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). A, being legally bound to appear before a High Court, in obedience to a subpoena issuing from that Court, intentionally omits to appear. A has committed the offence defined in this section

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 208 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

Illustration (b). A, being legally bound to appear before a District Judge, as a witness, in obedience to a summons issued by that District Judge intentionally omits to appear. A has committed the offence defined in this section

Exam use: quote illustration (b), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 208 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 208 (Non-attendance in obedience to an order from public servant), Chapter XIII — Of Contempts of the Lawful Authority of Public Servants.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever, being legally bound to attend in person or by an agent at a certain place and time in obedience to a summons, notice, order, or proclamation proceeding from any public servant legally competent, as such public servant, to issue the same, intentionally omits to attend at that place or time or departs from the place where he is bound to attend before the time at which it is lawful for him to depart,–
   (2) (a) shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both;
   (3) (b) where the summons, notice, order or proclamation is to attend in person or by agent in a Court with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 208 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 208 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.
